civilopediaText.text: An infantry regiment or brigade of about 3,000 men: three battalions of riflemen with machine guns, mortars and anti-tank weapons.
Infantry took and held the ground. In Normandy the hedgerows, sunken lanes and stone farms gave defenders cover every few hundred yards, so attacks across the open were costly.
Infantry can dig Foxholes.

name: Paratroopers
uniques: May Paradrop to [Land] tiles up to [5] tiles away <in [{Friendly} {Land}] tiles> <if [Normandy Scenario] is not constructed>

civilopediaText.text: Lightly armed infantry who jump from transport aircraft or land in gliders behind the enemy's front.

Scattered by the night drop, small groups fought their way to their objectives and held them until the seaborne troops arrived. Paratroopers slip past enemy positions (they ignore zones of control) and, from a city of their own, can be dropped up to five hexes away.
A regiment or battalion of fifty-odd medium tanks.
Tanks are fast and hit hard in open country, but the hedgerows hid anti-tank guns and infantry with Panzerfausts at a few yards' range.
Heavily armoured tanks with long-barrelled high-velocity guns.
Self-propelled anti-tank guns, built to knock out tanks rather than to lead an assault.

name: Field Artillery
uniques: Must set up to ranged attack

civilopediaText.text: Battalions of 105mm howitzers or 25-pounder gun-howitzers firing at targets their forward observers can see.
Towed anti-tank guns, dug in and camouflaged to ambush tanks at close range.

Fast escorts with 4.7- or 5-inch guns. Off Omaha Beach on the morning of D-Day, a dozen American and British destroyers steamed in so close that their keels scraped the bottom and shot up the German strongpoints at point-blank range.
Light and heavy cruisers with six-inch or eight-inch guns.
Battleships and monitors with 14- and 15-inch guns. Their shells could reach twenty miles inland, and German counterattacks near the coast were broken up by naval gunfire again and again.

The command ship of an assault force, packed with radios and staff officers - USS Bayfield (Utah), USS Ancon (Omaha), HMS Bulolo (Gold), HMS Hilary (Juno), HMS Largs (Sword). From here the naval and army commanders ran the landings.
It lies at anchor in its fleet's Transport Area for the whole battle and cannot move or fight.

name: General
uniques: [+15]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles
Can be earned through combat <for [Land] units>
Is part of Great Person group [General]

civilopediaText.text: A corps or division commander with his staff, signallers and jeeps.
A general inspires the troops near him (the best bonus in range applies; bonuses do not stack). Generals cannot be captured - if the enemy reaches one, he is lost.
Combat engineers with demolition charges, Bangalore torpedoes, mine detectors and bulldozers.
They blew gaps in the beach obstacles and the wire, cleared the minefields and built the roads off the beaches. Engineers fight at +50% against cities and build Foxholes and Roads.

name: Medics
uniques: All adjacent units heal [+15] HP when healing

civilopediaText.text: Aid men, stretcher bearers, ambulances and a field hospital. Adjacent units heal faster.
Trucks with ammunition, fuel and rations. It sets up a supply dump (a new city) where the army can raise and refit units.

name: US Infantry
uniques: [This Unit] gets a name from the [US Infantry] group

civilopediaText.text: An American infantry regiment, armed with the M1 Garand - the only semi-automatic rifle issued to a whole army - and the Browning Automatic Rifle: +10% Strength.
On D-Day the 4th Division landed at Utah almost unopposed, while the 1st and 29th Divisions fought for six hours to get off Omaha Beach.

name: British Infantry
uniques: [This Unit] gets a name from the [British Infantry] group

civilopediaText.text: A British infantry brigade of three battalions, with Lee-Enfield rifles and the Bren light machine gun at the heart of every section. Steady and dogged in defence: +15% Strength when defending.
The 50th (Northumbrian) Division landed on Gold Beach and the 3rd Division on Sword.

name: Canadian Infantry
uniques: [This Unit] gets a name from the [Canadian Infantry] group

civilopediaText.text: A brigade of the 3rd Canadian Division - all volunteers. On D-Day they stormed the seafront towns of Juno Beach under heavy fire, and by evening their tanks had driven further inland than any other Allied force: +15% Strength when attacking.

name: US Rangers
uniques: Eliminates combat penalty for attacking across a coast

civilopediaText.text: The 2nd and 5th Ranger Battalions, trained on the cliffs of the Isle of Wight. At 7:10 AM, three companies under Lt. Col. James Rudder fired rocket-propelled grapnels up the hundred-foot cliffs of Pointe du Hoc and climbed them under fire. 'Rangers, lead the way!' - General Cota's words to the 5th Rangers on Omaha Beach.
Rangers land without penalty (they disembark for one movement point and attack from the sea at full strength) and fight at +33% on cliffs.

name: Commandos
uniques: [This Unit] gets a name from the [Commandos] group
Eliminates combat penalty for attacking across a coast

civilopediaText.text: British Army and Royal Marine Commandos in their green berets, and Commandant Philippe Kieffer's 177 Free French commandos, the only French troops to land on D-Day.

Lord Lovat's 1st Special Service Brigade marched from Sword Beach to Pegasus Bridge behind his piper, Bill Millin; 47 Royal Marine Commando marched ten miles behind the German lines to take Port-en-Bessin. Commandos land without penalty, slip through enemy lines (they ignore zones of control) and fight at +25% against cities.

name: US Paratroopers
uniques: May Paradrop to [Land] tiles up to [5] tiles away <in [{Friendly} {Land}] tiles> <if [Normandy Scenario] is not constructed>
[This Unit] gets a name from the [US Paratroopers] group

civilopediaText.text: Parachute and glider infantry regiments of the 82nd and 101st Airborne Divisions - 13,000 men dropped over the Cotentin in the night. Scattered across miles of hedgerows and flooded fields, they gathered in small bands with their 'cricket' clickers and took Sainte-Mère-Église, the Utah causeways and the Merderet bridges.

name: British Paratroopers
uniques: May Paradrop to [Land] tiles up to [5] tiles away <in [{Friendly} {Land}] tiles> <if [Normandy Scenario] is not constructed>
[This Unit] gets a name from the [British Paratroopers] group

civilopediaText.text: The 6th Airborne Division - the 'Red Devils' of the 3rd and 5th Parachute Brigades and the 6th Airlanding Brigade - with the 1st Canadian Parachute Battalion. They seized the Orne bridges, silenced the Merville battery, blew the Dives bridges and held the high ground east of the Orne against every counterattack.

name: Sherman
uniques: [This Unit] gets a name from the [Sherman] group

civilopediaText.text: The M4 Sherman, the Allies' standard tank: reliable, fast and easy to repair, with a 75mm gun that fired a good high-explosive shell against infantry and guns (+10% vs infantry) but struggled against the front armour of the Panther.

name: DD Sherman
uniques: Eliminates combat penalty for attacking across a coast

civilopediaText.text: Duplex Drive 'swimming' Shermans, one of Major General Percy Hobart's 'Funnies': a canvas screen raised round the hull kept the tank afloat while two propellers drove it ashore from miles out.

Off Utah the 70th Tank Battalion's DD tanks were launched close in and nearly all landed. Off Omaha, launched far out into a heavy sea, 27 of the 741st Tank Battalion's 32 tanks sank. Afloat, a DD Sherman is as helpless as any landing craft; once ashore it drops its screen, fights as a Sherman and cannot go back to sea.

name: Sherman Firefly
uniques: [This Unit] gets a name from the [Sherman Firefly] group

civilopediaText.text: A British Sherman rearmed with the long 17-pounder gun, the only Allied tank gun that could reliably knock out a Panther or a Tiger: +50% vs armour. One in four British Shermans was a Firefly.
On the afternoon of D-Day the Staffordshire Yeomanry's Fireflies stopped the 21st Panzer Division's drive on the Périers ridge.

Armoured Vehicle Royal Engineers: heavily armoured Churchill tanks carrying a 290mm Petard spigot mortar that threw a 40-pound 'flying dustbin' against concrete, plus bridges, fascines and mat-layers.
Hobart's Funnies breached the sea wall and cracked the strongpoints on the British and Canadian beaches: +100% vs cities and +33% vs fortifications.

name: Cromwell
uniques: [This Unit] gets a name from the [Cromwell] group

civilopediaText.text: The fastest tank in Normandy, equipping the 7th Armoured Division - the 'Desert Rats' of North Africa, who began landing on Gold Beach on the evening of D-Day.

name: M10 Tank Destroyer
uniques: [This Unit] gets a name from the [M10 Tank Destroyer] group

civilopediaText.text: The open-topped M10 Wolverine with a three-inch gun. The 899th Tank Destroyer Battalion landed on Utah Beach on D-Day.

name: US Artillery
uniques: Must set up to ranged attack
Ranged attacks may be performed over obstacles
[This Unit] gets a name from the [US Artillery] group

civilopediaText.text: Battalions of 105mm howitzers with forward observers and the American fire direction centre, which could mass every gun in range on one target within minutes. Fires over obstacles.
On Omaha most of the divisional artillery was lost when the overloaded DUKWs carrying it swamped in the surf.

name: Royal Artillery
uniques: Ranged attacks may be performed over obstacles
[This Unit] gets a name from the [Royal Artillery] group

civilopediaText.text: Field regiments of the Royal Artillery and Royal Canadian Artillery. The assault divisions' guns were self-propelled - Sextons with 25-pounders and Priests with 105mm howitzers - and fired 'run-in shoots' from their landing craft as they approached the beaches. Self-propelled: no set-up needed. Fires over obstacles.

name: Allied Anti-Tank Guns
uniques: [This Unit] gets a name from the [Allied Anti-Tank Guns] group

civilopediaText.text: Anti-tank regiments with 6-pounder and 17-pounder guns. Brought ashore early, they and the Fireflies broke the 21st Panzer Division's counterattack on D-Day.

name: US General
uniques: [+15]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles
Can be earned through combat <for [Land] units>
Is part of Great Person group [General]
[This Unit] gets a name from the [US General] group

civilopediaText.text: An American corps or division commander. Named generals have personal abilities - see their promotions (for example Roosevelt, Cota, Gavin or Ridgway).

name: British General
uniques: [+15]% Strength bonus for [{Military} {Land}] units within [2] tiles
[This Unit] gets a name from the [British General] group

civilopediaText.text: A British or Canadian corps, division or brigade commander. Named generals have personal abilities - see their promotions (for example Montgomery, Gale or Lovat).

name: Combat Engineers
uniques: [This Unit] gets a name from the [Combat Engineers] group

civilopediaText.text: Engineer Special Brigades, Special Engineer Task Forces, Royal Engineers and Royal Canadian Engineers: the men who blew paths through the beach obstacles under fire, cleared the mines and bulldozed the exits off the beaches.
+50% vs cities; they build Foxholes and Roads.

name: Grenadiers
uniques: [This Unit] gets a name from the [Grenadiers] group

civilopediaText.text: A German grenadier regiment. Every section was built around the MG 42 machine gun, which fired twenty rounds a second: +15% Strength when defending.
The 352nd Division, a field division with many veterans of the Eastern Front, had moved up to the coast behind Omaha in March - Allied intelligence did not know it was there.
Panzerfausts and Panzerschrecks: +25% vs armour.
The garrisons of the Atlantic Wall: static divisions like the 709th and 716th, made up of older men, convalescents and conscripts, with few vehicles and a mixed bag of captured weapons.

They manned the Widerstandsnester - 'resistance nests' of bunkers, trenches, mines and wire - every half mile along the coast. Stubborn behind concrete (+33% when defending), poor in the attack (-20%).
Panzerfausts and Panzerschrecks: +25% vs armour.

Battalions of Soviet prisoners of war - Georgians, Armenians, Azerbaijanis, Russians and others - who had joined the German army, many simply to escape the starvation of the prison camps, and were posted to the West.
Some fought hard; many surrendered at the first chance. They often fall back before an assault.
Panzerfausts and Panzerschrecks: +25% vs armour.

name: Fallschirmjaeger
uniques: May Paradrop to [Land] tiles up to [5] tiles away <in [{Friendly} {Land}] tiles> <if [Normandy Scenario] is not constructed>

civilopediaText.text: German paratroopers - the Fallschirmjäger - who had not made a combat jump since Crete in 1941 but were among the best infantry in the German army.
Major Friedrich von der Heydte's 6th Fallschirmjäger Regiment, young and well armed, fought the 101st Airborne for Carentan for a week.
Panzerfausts and Panzerschrecks: +25% vs armour.

name: Panzergrenadiers
uniques: [This Unit] gets a name from the [Panzergrenadiers] group

civilopediaText.text: Motorised and armoured infantry of the panzer divisions, riding half-tracks and trucks. They move like tanks and attack hard (+15%).

The 12th SS Panzer Division's grenadiers were mostly eighteen-year-olds of the Hitler Youth, led by veterans of the Eastern Front; they fought the Canadians around Caen with great ferocity, and some of them murdered Canadian prisoners at Authie and the Abbaye d'Ardenne.
Panzerfausts and Panzerschrecks: +25% vs armour.

name: Panzer IV
uniques: [This Unit] gets a name from the [Panzer IV] group

civilopediaText.text: The Panzer IV with the long 75mm gun - the workhorse of the panzer divisions, slightly better armed than the Sherman: +15% vs armour. The 21st Panzer Division's 22nd Panzer Regiment, the only armour close to the beaches, had about 100 of them.

name: Panther
uniques: [This Unit] gets a name from the [Panther] group

civilopediaText.text: The Panzer V Panther: thick sloped frontal armour and a long, high-velocity 75mm gun that could destroy a Sherman at well over a mile. The 12th SS and Panzer Lehr Divisions each had a battalion of them.

name: StuG III
uniques: [This Unit] gets a name from the [StuG III] group

civilopediaText.text: Turretless assault guns and tank destroyers - StuG IIIs, Marders and Major Alfred Becker's home-made conversions of captured French tanks. Low and hard to spot, they were deadly ambushers in the hedgerows: +33% vs armour and +20% when defending.

name: German Artillery
uniques: Must set up to ranged attack
Ranged attacks may be performed over obstacles
[This Unit] gets a name from the [German Artillery] group

civilopediaText.text: Battalions of 105mm leFH 18 field howitzers. On D-Day the 352nd Division's guns had every exit off Omaha Beach registered. Major Werner Pluskat, watching from his bunker at dawn, saw the whole invasion fleet appear out of the mist. Fires over obstacles.

name: Nebelwerfer
uniques: Ranged attacks may be performed over obstacles
[This Unit] gets a name from the [Nebelwerfer] group

civilopediaText.text: Six-barrelled rocket launchers that fired a ripple of 150mm rockets with a terrifying howl - the Allied troops called them 'Moaning Minnies'. Devastating against troops in the open but inaccurate (-25% vs cities). They fired and moved off before the counter-battery fire arrived.

name: 88 Flak
uniques: [This Unit] gets a name from the [88 Flak] group

civilopediaText.text: The 88mm anti-aircraft gun, used in the ground role as the most feared anti-tank gun of the war: it could pierce any Allied tank at long range. III Flak Corps sent its batteries to Normandy as anti-tank screens.

Heavy coast-defence guns in concrete casemates: the navy's 150mm guns at Longues, the 210mm guns of the Crisbecq battery, the army's 155mm guns at Pointe du Hoc, the 100mm howitzers at Merville. Their casemates faced the sea: they fire only at ships and landing craft, three hexes out, and fight at +50% against warships. They cannot move.

Can be earned through combat <for [Land] units>
Is part of Great Person group [General]
[This Unit] gets a name from the [German General] group

civilopediaText.text: A German corps, division or regiment commander. Named commanders have personal abilities - see their promotions (for example Marcks, von der Heydte, von Luck or Bayerlein).

name: Pioniere
uniques: [This Unit] gets a name from the [Pioniere] group

civilopediaText.text: German combat engineers with mines, flamethrowers and demolition charges. +50% vs cities; they build Foxholes and Roads.
Panzerfausts and Panzerschrecks: +25% vs armour.
